posts.summary:
The General Services Administration's Federal Acquisition Service awarded Minburn Technology Group, LLC a blanket purchase agreement call under the GSA Multiple Award Schedule on November 18, 2026. The agreement, which became public two days later, carries an initial obligation of approximately $46.2 million against a ceiling of $151.1 million and runs through November 21, 2027. The work involves software publishing services, specifically business application and application development software as a service.

The award was made through full and open competition and is associated with subscription licenses for DOD365SEC. Minburn Technology Group will provide these services under the existing GSA MAS vehicle, which streamlines procurement for federal agencies seeking software and IT solutions.

posts.summary:
The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services awarded a task order to Nimbus Consulting LLC under the GSA Multiple Award Schedule to provide custom computer programming and application development support services. The work supports the Center for Program Integrity in advancing national health care transformation initiatives. The task order, which was set aside for small businesses and awarded through full and open competition, has an initial obligation of approximately $7.3 million against a ceiling of $36.7 million.

The task order runs from November 21, 2026, through November 20, 2027. This award was signed on November 20, 2026.

posts.summary:
The Department of Homeland Security's Office of Procurement Operations awarded Palantir Technologies Inc. a blanket purchase agreement call valued at approximately $32.1 million. The award, signed on September 29, 2026, supports the procurement of software-as-a-service licenses for business applications and application development. The agreement runs through September 29, 2027.

The award was made through full and open competition and falls under the software publishing industry classification. Palantir will provide licensing services to support the agency's information technology and telecommunications needs under this one-year performance period.
